findings.issue_text: CryptoIntegration.detectProvider silently resolves provider conflicts with undefined tie-breaking: full providers all have order()==200, so coexisting providers fall back to ServiceLoader classpath order, and a FIPS-configured deployment could silently get a non-FIPS provider
Fail-fast detection of a misconfigured classpath in detectProvider is converted into silent behavior, with no error or log indicating which provider won a previously-failing conflict
ASN1Decoder.readSequence mishandles indefinite-length (0x80 BER) encoding by returning an empty list instead of failing or parsing, since readLength returns -1 and the sentinel is not propagated

ASN1Decoder.readLength bounds check validates declared length against the whole buffer length instead of the unread remainder, causing valid boundary-case encodings to be rejected and invalid ones to produce misleading EOF errors
Dead/throwaway encoding work in concatenatedRSToASN1DER: two ASN1Encoder instances are created and discarded with output never used, suggesting an unfinished edit
getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default KeyStore's provider (usually SUN) instead of BouncyCastle, masking unsupported functionality that other methods surface via UnsupportedOperationException
AuthzClient.create(InputStream) and other construction paths may bypass create(Configuration) and skip CryptoIntegration.init, causing getProvider() to throw at first use

Silent provider resolution in CryptoIntegration masks misconfiguration; previously threw IllegalStateException for multiple CryptoProvider implementations, now silently picks highest-order() provider with only debug-level logging, risking wrong crypto provider in FIPS deployments
WildFlyElytronProvider.order() and DefaultCryptoProvider.order() are tied at 200, and ServiceLoader ordering is not deterministic, making provider selection environment-dependent

ASN1Decoder.readSequence() never verifies the total consumed bytes match the declared sequence length, allowing the parser to read past sequence boundaries and accept malformed/non-canonical DER signatures
ASN1Decoder.readInteger() accepts non-minimal INTEGER encodings (leading 0x00 padding in R/S) which are then silently normalized by integerToBytes(), enabling signature malleability
AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default KeyStore provider (typically Sun JCE) instead of BouncyCastle, returning a wrong-but-plausible value
ASN1Decoder.readLength() bounds check only validates long-form lengths against the whole input length, not element bounds or current position, permitting acceptance of malformed DER

AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() creates a new KeyStore (and does provider lookup) on every call, causing repeated allocation; it also returns the JDK default keystore's provider rather than BouncyCastle, a semantic mismatch
concatenatedRSToASN1DER constructs two throwaway ASN1Encoder instances whose encoded results are discarded — dead allocation on the per-signature hot path

writeDerSeq path in concatenatedRSToASN1DER double-materializes: concatenate() builds an intermediate ByteArrayOutputStream, copies to byte[], then writeEncoded re-encodes, adding O(n) extra copies per signature

ASN1Decoder.readSequence silently accepts indefinite-length BER encoding as empty/truncated sequence because readLength() returns -1 which the while (length > 0) loop treats as done, producing no clear error

CryptoIntegration.detectProvider non-deterministically selects a provider when multiple providers with equal order() (all 200) coexist, replacing a previous hard failure with silent classpath-order-dependent selection

AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JVM's default keystore provider (typically SUN) instead of BouncyCastle, causing silently wrong behavior for callers expecting BC semantics
AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getKeyStore uses format.name() while all other providers use format.toString(), which would break keystore loading if KeystoreFormat overrides toString()
CryptoIntegration.init is only wired into AuthzClient.create(Configuration) and not other entry points like create(InputStream), potentially skipping crypto init on those paths

Behavioral change in CryptoIntegration.detectProvider (multiple crypto providers no longer throw IllegalStateException, silently picks highest-order provider) has no test coverage for provider sorting and the removed error path
No test that AuthzClient.create() initializes AuthzClientCryptoProvider via ServiceLoader (service-file lookup only exercised by direct instantiation)
ECDSAAlgorithmTest round-trip conversion test is self-referential and cannot detect symmetric encoding bugs; should verify ASN.1 DER output with Signature.verify or known test vectors
Test key curve not pinned to algorithm under test; a single EC key (P-256) means integerToBytes truncation path is never exercised for ES384/ES512
No edge-case tests for ASN1Decoder on malformed/truncated input such as indefinite-length encoding, out-of-bounds lengths, and high-tag-number forms
Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER: two ASN1Encoder instances are created and their output discarded

Hand-rolled ASN.1 DER encoder/decoder (ASN1Decoder.java, ASN1Encoder.java) duplicates existing Keycloak ECDSACryptoProvider logic, creating three divergent implementations where bugs fixed in one copy won't propagate

Hand-written DER parsing is error-prone and lifted nearly verbatim from BouncyCastle's ASN1InputStream minus safety checks (e.g., mark() uses is.available() as mark limit, only coincidentally valid for ByteArrayInputStream)
Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER: two ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) statements create encoders, write, and immediately discard the results
getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JCA KeyStore default provider (typically SUN) instead of the BouncyCastle provider, breaking callers relying on the method contract

SPI resource file registering CryptoProvider lives in wrong module (authz-client), creating implicit classpath coupling that silently adds a second provider and causes confusing UnsupportedOperationException instead of the previous clear 'multiple providers' error
CryptoIntegration.detectProvider replaces fail-fast IllegalStateException with a sorted pick plus debug log, hiding classpath misconfigurations
Two providers with equal order() (e.g., default and elytron both = 200) resolve arbitrarily by ServiceLoader order, causing nondeterministic provider selection across classloaders
'Ignored crypto providers' log message uses logger.debugf(builder.toString()) with no format specifiers and leaves a trailing ', ', risking IllegalFormatException patterns

About 15 of ~20 interface methods in AuthzClientCryptoProvider throw UnsupportedOperationException, a leaky partial implementation of the SPI that fails at runtime rather than compile time; should narrow the abstraction

~90-line anonymous inner class with private helpers (integerToBytes) inside getEcdsaCryptoProvider() mixes provider plumbing with algorithm implementation and duplicates integerToBytes logic from other Keycloak ECDSA providers; should be a named shared class
ECDSAAlgorithmTest only checks round-trip rather than correctness against known-good fixed vectors, which can mask symmetric encoding bugs (e.g., DER length bugs that cancel out)

Silent provider downgrade in CryptoIntegration.detectProvider: multiple CryptoProviders no longer fail fast; equal order() values (200) between DefaultCryptoProvider and FIPS1402Provider make winner nondeterministic, potentially running non-FIPS BouncyCastle with only debug-level logging (FIPS bypass risk)

ASN1Decoder.readSequence silently returns empty list for indefinite-length encoding because readLength returns -1 and the while(length > 0) loop is skipped, accepting malformed BER input without error

ASN1Decoder.readLength bounds check uses the entire input array size as limit rather than remaining sequence content; length accounting can go negative without error and the loop silently stops on inconsistent lengths
AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JVM's default keystore provider (KeyStore.getDefaultType()) instead of BouncyCastle, violating the method contract
CryptoIntegration.init is only called in the create(Configuration) overload of AuthzClient but not create(InputStream) or no-arg create(), so provider registration may not happen on those paths
Adding non-default order() method to CryptoProvider breaks binary compatibility for third-party implementations, throwing AbstractMethodError during provider sorting; should be a default method
ASN1Decoder mark(is.available()) and count-based header math is fragile if fed a non-ByteArrayInputStream-backed stream (latent issue)

adjudication_records.issue_text: CryptoIntegration.detectProvider silently resolves provider conflicts with undefined tie-breaking: full providers all have order()==200, so coexisting providers fall back to ServiceLoader classpath order, and a FIPS-configured deployment could silently get a non-FIPS provider
Fail-fast detection of a misconfigured classpath in detectProvider is converted into silent behavior, with no error or log indicating which provider won a previously-failing conflict

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the previous fail-fast exception when multiple CryptoProviders are found (the IllegalStateException block was deleted), but it is not “silent”: `detectProvider` now logs the winning provider via `logger.debugf("Detected crypto provider: %s", ...)` and also logs the other providers as “Ignored crypto providers: ...”. So the claim that there is “no error or log indicating which provider won” is contradicted by the added debug logging.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.readSequence mishandles indefinite-length (0x80 BER) encoding by returning an empty list instead of failing or parsing, since readLength returns -1 and the sentinel is not propagated
matched_golden_ids: When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same root problem: indefinite-length BER encoding yields a length of -1, and the decoder does not correctly handle/propagate this sentinel. The golden highlights incorrect arithmetic with -1, while the candidate describes the resulting misbehavior in readSequence (treating -1 as a normal length and producing an empty list instead of proper parsing/failure).

adjudication_records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.readLength bounds check validates declared length against the whole buffer length instead of the unread remainder, causing valid boundary-case encodings to be rejected and invalid ones to produce misleading EOF errors

adjudication.rationale: In ASN1Decoder.readLength(), the check `if (length >= limit)` compares against the total buffer length (`limit = bytes.length`), which is looser than comparing against the unread remainder (`limit - count`). That means it would fail to catch some out-of-bounds declared lengths early and can indeed lead to later EOF errors, but it would not reject valid boundary-case encodings more often; the opposite is true (it under-validates). The finding’s core claim about rejecting valid encodings due to this check is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead/throwaway encoding work in concatenatedRSToASN1DER: two ASN1Encoder instances are created and discarded with output never used, suggesting an unfinished edit
getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default KeyStore's provider (usually SUN) instead of BouncyCastle, masking unsupported functionality that other methods surface via UnsupportedOperationException
matched_golden_ids: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly states that getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default KeyStore provider (e.g., SUN) instead of BouncyCastle, which is the same underlying issue as the golden comment about returning the wrong provider (default keystore vs BouncyCastle).

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClient.create(InputStream) and other construction paths may bypass create(Configuration) and skip CryptoIntegration.init, causing getProvider() to throw at first use

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows CryptoIntegration.init(...) being added in AuthzClient.create(Configuration). It does not show the implementation of AuthzClient.create(InputStream) or any other construction paths that would bypass create(Configuration) (e.g., a public constructor or other factory methods calling `new AuthzClient(...)` directly). Without those code paths in the diff, the claim that they “bypass” and “skip init” is not verifiable from what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent provider resolution in CryptoIntegration masks misconfiguration; previously threw IllegalStateException for multiple CryptoProvider implementations, now silently picks highest-order() provider with only debug-level logging, risking wrong crypto provider in FIPS deployments

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes CryptoIntegration.detectProvider() to no longer throw when multiple CryptoProvider implementations are present; it now sorts by CryptoProvider::order (descending) and returns the first, only logging the rest at debug level. This can mask misconfiguration and potentially select the wrong provider. The risk is amplified because multiple built-in providers in this diff (DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, FIPS1402Provider) all return the same order() value (200), so selection among them becomes dependent on ServiceLoader iteration order (not guaranteed), making provider choice potentially nondeterministic and possibly incorrect for FIPS-sensitive deployments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: WildFlyElytronProvider.order() and DefaultCryptoProvider.order() are tied at 200, and ServiceLoader ordering is not deterministic, making provider selection environment-dependent

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes CryptoIntegration.detectProvider to sort providers only by `CryptoProvider::order` (descending) and then pick the first, even when multiple providers are present (it now just logs the rest). In the same diff, `DefaultCryptoProvider.order()` and `WildFlyElytronProvider.order()` (and also `FIPS1402Provider.order()`) all return `200`, so ties are not broken deterministically by the comparator. With equal `order`, which provider ends up first depends on the underlying `ServiceLoader` iteration order, so selection can vary if more than one of these is on the classpath.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.readSequence() never verifies the total consumed bytes match the declared sequence length, allowing the parser to read past sequence boundaries and accept malformed/non-canonical DER signatures

adjudication.rationale: In ASN1Decoder.readSequence(), the declared SEQUENCE length is tracked via `length`, but the loop only checks `while (length > 0)` and never enforces that each child TLV fits within the remaining bytes or that the final `length` ends exactly at 0. Since `readNext()` reads a full TLV from the underlying stream regardless of the remaining `length`, an element can consume more bytes than the SEQUENCE’s declared length (making `length` negative) and the method will still return successfully after having read past the SEQUENCE boundary. This can cause acceptance of malformed/non-canonical encodings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.readInteger() accepts non-minimal INTEGER encodings (leading 0x00 padding in R/S) which are then silently normalized by integerToBytes(), enabling signature malleability

adjudication.rationale: The new ECDSA conversion logic parses DER signatures using ASN1Decoder.readInteger(), which simply constructs a BigInteger from the INTEGER octets without enforcing DER-minimal integer encoding (e.g., rejecting unnecessary leading 0x00 padding). In AuthzClientCryptoProvider.asn1derToConcatenatedRS(), the parsed BigIntegers are then canonicalized to fixed-size via integerToBytes() (cropping/padding), meaning distinct non-canonical INTEGER encodings can normalize to the same (r,s) byte sequence. This violates the implied “DER” contract of asn1derToConcatenatedRS and creates a malleability/canonicalization issue in the parser as implemented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default KeyStore provider (typically Sun JCE) instead of BouncyCastle, returning a wrong-but-plausible value

adjudication.rationale: In `AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider()`, the implementation returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, i.e., the provider backing the JVM's default keystore type (typically a Sun/Oracle provider), not a BouncyCastle `Provider`. This contradicts the `CryptoProvider` contract (`getBouncyCastleProvider()`) and can lead to incorrect behavior if callers rely on it being the BC provider.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.readLength() bounds check only validates long-form lengths against the whole input length, not element bounds or current position, permitting acceptance of malformed DER

adjudication.rationale: In ASN1Decoder.readLength(), the only upper-bound validation for long-form lengths is `if (length >= limit)` where `limit` is the total byte[] size passed to the decoder, not the remaining bytes in the current context (e.g., remaining bytes inside the enclosing SEQUENCE). Then readSequence() trusts the SEQUENCE's declared `length` but does not enforce that each nested element's TLV fits within the remaining SEQUENCE length; it just subtracts `bytes.length` after reading the element, allowing `length` to go negative without error and still returning successfully. This can accept DER encodings where an inner element extends beyond the SEQUENCE's declared length (malformed DER).

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() creates a new KeyStore (and does provider lookup) on every call, causing repeated allocation; it also returns the JDK default keystore's provider rather than BouncyCastle, a semantic mismatch

adjudication.rationale: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider(), the implementation is `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`. This both (a) instantiates/looks up a KeyStore on every call and (b) returns the provider backing the JDK default keystore type (e.g., SUN/PKCS12), not a BouncyCastle provider, despite the method contract/name being specifically “getBouncyCastleProvider()”. That is a verifiable semantic mismatch in the diff and can lead to incorrect behavior if callers expect an actual BC provider.

adjudication_records.issue_text: concatenatedRSToASN1DER constructs two throwaway ASN1Encoder instances whose encoded results are discarded — dead allocation on the per-signature hot path
matched_golden_ids: Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that concatenatedRSToASN1DER creates ASN1Encoder instances whose outputs are discarded, describing them as throwaway/dead allocations. This matches the golden issue that earlier ASN1Encoder writes are unused because encoding is actually done by new ASN1Encoder instances in the return statement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: writeDerSeq path in concatenatedRSToASN1DER double-materializes: concatenate() builds an intermediate ByteArrayOutputStream, copies to byte[], then writeEncoded re-encodes, adding O(n) extra copies per signature

adjudication.rationale: In `AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getEcdsaCryptoProvider().concatenatedRSToASN1DER`, the call `ASN1Encoder.create().writeDerSeq( ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger), ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger))` goes through `ASN1Encoder.writeDerSeq`, which calls `concatenate(objects)` to build a temporary `ByteArrayOutputStream` and then `tmp.toByteArray()`, and then `writeEncoded(...)` writes that byte[] into another `ByteArrayOutputStream` (`os`). This does create an intermediate buffer + copy (extra O(n) per signature) but is a performance/efficiency concern, not a correctness/security defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.readSequence silently accepts indefinite-length BER encoding as empty/truncated sequence because readLength() returns -1 which the while (length > 0) loop treats as done, producing no clear error

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added ASN1Decoder, readLength() explicitly returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding (length == 0x80). readSequence() then does `while (length > 0)` and will therefore skip parsing entirely when length is -1, returning an empty List without throwing. This silently accepts BER indefinite-length sequences (or malformed input) as empty/truncated rather than rejecting or correctly handling end-of-contents markers, which is a real correctness/security defect in the added logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CryptoIntegration.detectProvider non-deterministically selects a provider when multiple providers with equal order() (all 200) coexist, replacing a previous hard failure with silent classpath-order-dependent selection

adjudication.rationale: In CryptoIntegration.detectProvider, the previous hard-failure on multiple providers (`else if (foundProviders.size() > 1) throw ...`) was removed. Now providers are sorted only by `order()` descending and the first is returned, while the rest are merely logged as ignored. Since DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return the same `order()` value (200), there is no explicit tie-breaker in the comparator, so selection among equal-order providers depends on the iteration order from `ServiceLoader.load(...)` (i.e., classpath/service discovery order). This makes the chosen provider ambiguous and potentially classpath-order-dependent rather than failing fast.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JVM's default keystore provider (typically SUN) instead of BouncyCastle, causing silently wrong behavior for callers expecting BC semantics

adjudication.rationale: In the new `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, `getBouncyCastleProvider()` is implemented as `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which returns the provider for the JVM default keystore type (commonly a SUN/Oracle provider), not BouncyCastle. Given the `CryptoProvider` interface method is explicitly named/defined to return a BouncyCastle provider, this implementation is incorrect and can lead to callers getting a non-BC provider without any signal.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getKeyStore uses format.name() while all other providers use format.toString(), which would break keystore loading if KeystoreFormat overrides toString()

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getKeyStore() calling KeyStore.getInstance(format.name()), while other CryptoProvider implementations in the diff (e.g., FIPS1402Provider) use format.toString(). This is a real inconsistency and could lead to different keystore type strings if KeystoreFormat.toString() is customized, but the diff does not show KeystoreFormat overriding toString(), so the claim that it "would break" is not fully verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CryptoIntegration.init is only wired into AuthzClient.create(Configuration) and not other entry points like create(InputStream), potentially skipping crypto init on those paths

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader());` being added inside `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)`. It does not show the implementation of `create(InputStream)` (beyond its signature), nor how it delegates internally. From the diff alone, you can’t verify that `create(InputStream)` (or other entry points) bypass `create(Configuration)` and therefore “skip crypto init.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavioral change in CryptoIntegration.detectProvider (multiple crypto providers no longer throw IllegalStateException, silently picks highest-order provider) has no test coverage for provider sorting and the removed error path

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes CryptoIntegration.detectProvider to (a) sort ServiceLoader results by CryptoProvider::order descending and (b) no longer throw when multiple providers are present, instead selecting the first and only logging ignored providers (common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java). The diff also introduces the new CryptoProvider.order() API and assigns values in implementations. However, the only added test is ECDSAAlgorithmTest, which exercises ECDSA signature conversions via AuthzClientCryptoProvider; there is no test added covering provider sorting/selection behavior or the removed IllegalStateException path when multiple providers are on the classpath.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test that AuthzClient.create() initializes AuthzClientCryptoProvider via ServiceLoader (service-file lookup only exercised by direct instantiation)

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader())` to `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)` and registers `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` via `META-INF/services/org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider`, implying ServiceLoader-based discovery should work when creating an `AuthzClient`. The only new test (`ECDSAAlgorithmTest`) instantiates `new AuthzClientCryptoProvider()` directly and never calls `AuthzClient.create(...)` nor exercises `CryptoIntegration`/ServiceLoader lookup, so there is no test coverage for the intended initialization path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ECDSAAlgorithmTest round-trip conversion test is self-referential and cannot detect symmetric encoding bugs; should verify ASN.1 DER output with Signature.verify or known test vectors

adjudication.rationale: In ECDSAAlgorithmTest, the assertion only checks that prov.getEcdsaCryptoProvider().asn1derToConcatenatedRS() and concatenatedRSToASN1DER() are inverse of each other for the produced signature bytes (DER -> RS -> DER -> RS, then compare RS arrays). Because both transformations come from the same new implementation (AuthzClientCryptoProvider + ASN1Encoder/ASN1Decoder), a symmetric/paired bug (e.g., wrong handling of leading zero/sign bit, truncation/padding rules, or swapped r/s) could still round-trip and make the test pass without proving the DER output is valid for Signature.verify or matches known vectors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test key curve not pinned to algorithm under test; a single EC key (P-256) means integerToBytes truncation path is never exercised for ES384/ES512

adjudication.rationale: In ECDSAAlgorithmTest, the KeyPair is generated once via KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair() without specifying a curve. This commonly yields a P-256 key, yet the same key is used for ES256/ES384/ES512 tests while passing algorithm.getSignatureLength() into asn1derToConcatenatedRS/concatenatedRSToASN1DER. In AuthzClientCryptoProvider.integerToBytes, ES384/ES512 with a P-256-derived r/s will exercise the qLength > bytes.length padding branch, but not the qLength < bytes.length truncation branch the finding mentions. So the test is not pinned to the algorithm’s expected curve and provides incomplete/possibly misleading coverage for the new conversion logic, but it’s not a production defect shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No edge-case tests for ASN1Decoder on malformed/truncated input such as indefinite-length encoding, out-of-bounds lengths, and high-tag-number forms

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new nontrivial parsing logic in `ASN1Decoder` (e.g., `readLength()` handling indefinite-length `0x80`, bounds checks, and `readTagNumber()` high-tag-number parsing), but the only added test (`ECDSAAlgorithmTest`) exercises only valid DER signatures via round-trip conversion. There are no tests covering malformed/truncated inputs or edge cases (indefinite-length encoding, out-of-bounds lengths, invalid high-tag-number forms), so the finding about missing edge-case tests is accurate and grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER: two ASN1Encoder instances are created and their output discarded

adjudication.rationale: In `AuthzClientCryptoProvider#getEcdsaCryptoProvider().concatenatedRSToASN1DER`, the lines `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` instantiate encoders, write to their internal buffers, and then discard them without using the output. The method then correctly builds the DER sequence using new encoder instances in the `writeDerSeq(...)` call, so the extra two calls are redundant dead code (wasted allocations/IO) but not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hand-rolled ASN.1 DER encoder/decoder (ASN1Decoder.java, ASN1Encoder.java) duplicates existing Keycloak ECDSACryptoProvider logic, creating three divergent implementations where bugs fixed in one copy won't propagate

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new, self-contained ASN.1 DER encoder/decoder (authz/client/.../ASN1Encoder.java, ASN1Decoder.java) and wires it into a new CryptoProvider implementation (AuthzClientCryptoProvider#getEcdsaCryptoProvider) for ECDSA signature format conversion. This introduces a separate implementation of DER parsing/encoding logic in the authz-client module rather than reusing shared/common crypto utilities, creating a maintainability/architecture risk where fixes/improvements in other CryptoProvider/ECDSA handling won’t automatically apply to this copy. The exact claim of "three" existing implementations isn’t verifiable from this diff alone, but the added duplication risk is real and grounded in the new files and provider wiring.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hand-written DER parsing is error-prone and lifted nearly verbatim from BouncyCastle's ASN1InputStream minus safety checks (e.g., mark() uses is.available() as mark limit, only coincidentally valid for ByteArrayInputStream)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a bespoke ASN.1 DER encoder/decoder (ASN1Decoder/ASN1Encoder) rather than using a battle-tested implementation, which is a reasonable review concern about robustness/maintenance. In particular, ASN1Decoder.mark() calls is.mark(is.available()), which only “works” because the implementation hard-wires a ByteArrayInputStream (whose mark/reset behavior doesn’t depend on the readAheadLimit); if this logic were ever reused with a different InputStream, using available() as a mark limit would be unreliable. However, as shown, it’s not a verifiable functional defect because ASN1Decoder always wraps a byte[] in ByteArrayInputStream and the parsing is constrained to that.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER: two ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) statements create encoders, write, and immediately discard the results

adjudication.rationale: In `AuthzClientCryptoProvider#getEcdsaCryptoProvider().concatenatedRSToASN1DER`, the lines `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` each create a new encoder, write into it, and then discard it without using the result. The actual returned value is built by a separate `ASN1Encoder.create().writeDerSeq(ASN1Encoder.create().write(...), ...)` call. This is redundant/dead code (unnecessary allocations), but it does not change correctness of the returned signature encoding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JCA KeyStore default provider (typically SUN) instead of the BouncyCastle provider, breaking callers relying on the method contract

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, `getBouncyCastleProvider()` returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()` (i.e., the provider for the default JCA KeyStore type, typically SUN/Oracle), not a BouncyCastle (or BC-FIPS) provider. This differs from existing `CryptoProvider` implementations in the diff (e.g., `DefaultCryptoProvider`/`FIPS1402Provider`) which return an actual BC provider instance, and it violates the apparent contract implied by the method name/signature (`getBouncyCastleProvider`). Callers expecting BC-specific behavior could break when this provider is selected (and `AuthzClient.create` now calls `CryptoIntegration.init(...)`, enabling provider selection for authz-client).

adjudication_records.issue_text: SPI resource file registering CryptoProvider lives in wrong module (authz-client), creating implicit classpath coupling that silently adds a second provider and causes confusing UnsupportedOperationException instead of the previous clear 'multiple providers' error

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an SPI registration in the authz-client module (`authz/client/src/main/resources/META-INF/services/org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider` -> `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`) and also changes `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` to no longer fail when multiple providers are present (it now sorts by `CryptoProvider::order` and silently ignores the rest). That does create classpath coupling and removes the previous clear "multiple providers loaded" error. However, the specific claim that this will "cause confusing UnsupportedOperationException" is not directly verifiable from the diff: the new provider has a lower `order()` (100) than the existing providers (200), so when both are present it should be ignored rather than selected, and whether any code path hits its many `UnsupportedOperationException` methods is not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CryptoIntegration.detectProvider replaces fail-fast IllegalStateException with a sorted pick plus debug log, hiding classpath misconfigurations

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows CryptoIntegration.detectProvider() no longer throws when multiple CryptoProvider implementations are found. Instead it sorts by `CryptoProvider::order` (descending) and returns the first provider, only logging ignored providers at debug level (common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java). This does indeed hide the previous fail-fast signal for classpath/provider misconfiguration and can lead to non-obvious selection, especially when multiple providers share the same `order()` (all built-in providers in this diff return 200), in which case selection depends on ServiceLoader iteration order.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Two providers with equal order() (e.g., default and elytron both = 200) resolve arbitrarily by ServiceLoader order, causing nondeterministic provider selection across classloaders

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes provider selection from failing on multiple providers to selecting the first provider after sorting by `CryptoProvider::order` descending (`CryptoIntegration.detectProvider`). However, multiple built-in providers are updated to return the same `order()` value (DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, FIPS1402Provider all return 200). With equal keys, the sort provides no deterministic tie-breaker beyond the ServiceLoader encounter order, so which provider becomes `foundProviders.get(0)` can vary depending on ServiceLoader iteration/classpath ordering. This introduces potentially nondeterministic crypto provider selection when multiple providers are present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 'Ignored crypto providers' log message uses logger.debugf(builder.toString()) with no format specifiers and leaves a trailing ', ', risking IllegalFormatException patterns

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `logger.debugf(builder.toString());` in `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider`. While `debugf` treats the argument as a format string, the constructed message is constant text plus Java class names and commas (no format specifiers are introduced by this code), so there’s no verifiable `IllegalFormatException` risk from the diff itself. The trailing ", " is only a cosmetic logging issue, not a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: About 15 of ~20 interface methods in AuthzClientCryptoProvider throw UnsupportedOperationException, a leaky partial implementation of the SPI that fails at runtime rather than compile time; should narrow the abstraction

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `AuthzClientCryptoProvider implements CryptoProvider`, registers it via `META-INF/services/org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider`, and implements `order()` but leaves most SPI methods as `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet.")` (e.g., `getAlgorithmProvider`, `getCertificateUtils`, `getPemUtils`, `getSignature`, etc.). This is a real, diff-grounded concern because if this provider is ever selected by `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider(...)` (which now picks the highest `order()`), any caller invoking those SPI methods will fail at runtime. However, the diff does not show an actual code path in this PR that calls any of the unsupported methods, so it’s not a verifiable immediate defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ~90-line anonymous inner class with private helpers (integerToBytes) inside getEcdsaCryptoProvider() mixes provider plumbing with algorithm implementation and duplicates integerToBytes logic from other Keycloak ECDSA providers; should be a named shared class

adjudication.rationale: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider#getEcdsaCryptoProvider(), the diff adds a fairly large anonymous ECDSACryptoProvider implementation containing nontrivial algorithm logic (DER/RS conversions) and a private helper method integerToBytes(...) inside the anonymous class. This does mix provider plumbing (CryptoProvider implementation) with algorithm implementation details and makes reuse/testing harder. However, the claim that it "duplicates integerToBytes logic from other Keycloak ECDSA providers" cannot be verified from this diff alone, so the actionable, diff-grounded part is the architecture/maintainability concern, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ECDSAAlgorithmTest only checks round-trip rather than correctness against known-good fixed vectors, which can mask symmetric encoding bugs (e.g., DER length bugs that cancel out)

adjudication.rationale: The newly added `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` (authz/client/src/test/java/.../ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java) only asserts a DER→RS-concat→DER→RS-concat round-trip (`Assert.assertArrayEquals(rsConcat, rsConcat2)`). This can miss paired/symmetric bugs in the new ASN.1 conversion code (`ASN1Decoder`/`ASN1Encoder` used by `AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getEcdsaCryptoProvider()`), e.g., incorrect DER length handling or integer encoding issues that cancel out when encoding and decoding with the same implementation. No fixed known-good test vectors or independent verification of the produced DER bytes is present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent provider downgrade in CryptoIntegration.detectProvider: multiple CryptoProviders no longer fail fast; equal order() values (200) between DefaultCryptoProvider and FIPS1402Provider make winner nondeterministic, potentially running non-FIPS BouncyCastle with only debug-level logging (FIPS bypass risk)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes CryptoIntegration.detectProvider to no longer fail when multiple CryptoProvider implementations are found; instead it sorts by CryptoProvider::order (descending) and returns the first, only logging the rest at debug level. Multiple providers now implement order() with the same value (200 in DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider), so the “winner” among equal-order providers is not determined by this code and depends on ServiceLoader iteration order/classpath, which is not guaranteed. This can lead to unintended selection (including non-FIPS vs FIPS) without a hard failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.readSequence silently returns empty list for indefinite-length encoding because readLength returns -1 and the while(length > 0) loop is skipped, accepting malformed BER input without error

adjudication.rationale: In `ASN1Decoder.readSequence()`, it calls `int length = readLength();` and then loops `while (length > 0)`. `readLength()` explicitly returns `-1` for indefinite-length encoding (`if (length == 0x80) { return -1; }`). With `length == -1`, the loop is skipped and `readSequence()` returns an empty `List<byte[]>` without throwing, which is silent acceptance of an unsupported/invalid (for DER) encoding. This behavior is directly verifiable from the added `ASN1Decoder` code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.readLength bounds check uses the entire input array size as limit rather than remaining sequence content; length accounting can go negative without error and the loop silently stops on inconsistent lengths

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added ASN1Decoder.readSequence(), the loop decrements the declared SEQUENCE content length by each element’s total encoded length (bytes.length). If an element’s encoding exceeds the remaining declared length, `length` becomes negative and the loop exits without throwing, silently accepting an internally inconsistent SEQUENCE length. This matches the finding that length accounting can go negative without error. Additionally, readLength() only checks `length >= limit` where `limit` is the total input byte array size for that decoder, not the remaining bytes in the current SEQUENCE content, so it doesn’t enforce SEQUENCE-bound length correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JVM's default keystore provider (KeyStore.getDefaultType()) instead of BouncyCastle, violating the method contract

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, `getBouncyCastleProvider()` is implemented as `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which returns the provider for the JVM’s default keystore type (e.g., SUN/PKCS12), not BouncyCastle. The `CryptoProvider` interface method is explicitly documented as “Get BouncyCastle provider.” Returning an unrelated provider can break callers that rely on this contract (and `CryptoIntegration` can select this provider when it’s the only one on the classpath).

adjudication_records.issue_text: CryptoIntegration.init is only called in the create(Configuration) overload of AuthzClient but not create(InputStream) or no-arg create(), so provider registration may not happen on those paths

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader());` being added to `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)`. It does not show the bodies of `create(InputStream)` or any no-arg `create()`, so you cannot verify from this diff whether those overloads fail to initialize crypto (they may delegate to `create(Configuration)` or already call init elsewhere). The finding asserts a specific call-path omission that is not provable from the provided hunks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding non-default order() method to CryptoProvider breaks binary compatibility for third-party implementations, throwing AbstractMethodError during provider sorting; should be a default method
matched_golden_ids: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag that introducing an abstract/non-default order() method on CryptoProvider will break backward/binary compatibility for existing third-party implementations (e.g., causing AbstractMethodError) and implies it should be default to avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder mark(is.available()) and count-based header math is fragile if fed a non-ByteArrayInputStream-backed stream (latent issue)

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `ASN1Decoder` is explicitly backed by a `ByteArrayInputStream` constructed from a `byte[]` in its constructor (`private final ByteArrayInputStream is;` and `is = new ByteArrayInputStream(bytes);`). There is no code path allowing a non-`ByteArrayInputStream` stream to be provided, so the concern about fragility “if fed a non-ByteArrayInputStream-backed stream” is not grounded in the shown changes.
